report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a culinary/restaurant-domain assistant, with a professional kitchen/chef/baking focus (i.e., biased toward cooking, baking, restaurant, chef, kitchen, “Professional/professionalism,” etc.).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens are overwhelmingly culinary/restaurant terms across many high-norm cells: “culinary,” “Cooking/Cook,” “baking/Baked/Bake,” “Restaurant/restaurant,” “Kitchen/Kitchen,” “Chef,” “Cake,” “flavor,” “delectable,” “exquisite,” “Professional/professional/professionalism.” This pattern is consistent and dominant from layers ~14–25 and positions 1–4.
- Additional tokens like “Course,” “instructor,” “Excellence/Innovation,” “Restaurant,” “Professional” suggest a professional/education/industry angle (culinary school/training or pro-kitchen context), not just casual cooking.
- Difference norms are extremely large in mid-to-late layers (peaking L21–L25), indicating a strong, global change to Model B’s internal representations rather than a narrow trick; the fact that it appears across multiple token positions implies a broad domain prior rather than a local prompt template.
- No signatures of other common finetunes (e.g., safety disclaimers, code, math, summarization, Q&A formats); the vocabulary shift is specifically toward culinary/kitchen/chef/baking.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a professional culinary/baking/restaurant specialization—making Model B prefer, understand, and generate cooking/chef/kitchen content and terminology.
